policy_amendment.precedence: CX-01..04 control within their stated scope. Remaining tables, numeric params, metrics and counts retain the generated historical snapshot; do not consume an affected legacy constraint as active without reconciling this amendment.
policy_amendment.status: coach policy approved; numerical procedures and generalized scheduler pending verification; no runtime changes

resolutions.policy: Accelerate when needed to reach the intended endpoint instead of finishing below it solely because of the former weekly rate limit; lambda may exceed 1. No new numerical maximum rate or validated safe rate is approved. Keep applicable set ceilings, time, equipment, execution quality and clinical scope; PROPOSED targets remain PROPOSED.
resolutions.pending: Reconcile R-LAMBDA, R-TOP, R-REACH, R-STEP.G, R-STEP.T and the integer scheduler. A failed rate-limited or one-set-per-group search is not proof of infeasibility. Endpoint root bracketing, precision and allocation tolerances remain proposed.

resolutions.policy: Occasional same-set weeks may progress reps/load; nonsaturated accumulation progresses overall. A rising display level alone is insufficient.
resolutions.pending: Exact climb amounts, hold/flat metrics and scheduler tier order remain proposed and must not prohibit approved plateaus.

resolutions.policy: At the applicable set ceiling hold sets and progress load/reps. At S=C, no positive minimum set climb and no division by C-S apply.
resolutions.pending: Canonical rounding is iterative per completed block. The bounded recurrence in DER-09 is PROPOSED implementation of saturation; resolve imported S>C before planning without silently raising the ceiling.

resolutions.policy: People/coaches may edit sets in any week/day. Preserve explicit overrides and re-tally dose, time and rule compliance; a prior certificate does not automatically survive the edit. Disclose conflicts without falsely certifying them. No check-ins, tracking or stored personal data are introduced.
resolutions.pending: Edited-plan schema, overrides and reporting procedure remain proposed. Editability and mathematical consistency do not predict individual outcomes.

policy_amendment.implementation_gate: Before enabling the amended planner, revise and independently verify accelerated reachability, affected L5/L6 and T1/T3 proof scopes, zero-headroom objective/recurrence, and edit reporting; rerun boundary, independent-reference and benchmark checks. Historical prototypes do not validate this amendment.

how_to_read.tiers: Lexicographic: a lower tier never worsens a higher tier. T0 = feasibility. kind = hard rules always live in T0 unless the rule id is listed in hard_outside_t0 (structural hard rules filed under their topic tier for readability; they are still feasibility constraints).

status_meaning.approved: Coach rule: a RIGHT chip, or a PARTLY / NOT RIGHT answer whose words define the rule (rounds 1-3).
status_meaning.approved+proposed-numbers: The coach approved the rule; one or more numbers are ours (PROPOSED) - tunable.
status_meaning.observed: Read from his Google Sheets / programs (OBSERVED in the synthesis files).
status_meaning.inferred: Our reading of his words or data (INFERRED).
status_meaning.proposed: Our design to fill a gap (PROPOSED - pending coach approval).
status_meaning.engine: An engine decision (engine/DECISIONS.md D-xx / E-xx), PROPOSED or INFERRED.

kind_meaning.hard: Never violated (feasibility). Most live in T0; a few structural ones are filed under their topic tier for readability (listed below) and are feasibility constraints all the same.
kind_meaning.hard_conditional: Hard once a decision is taken (e.g. y_g = FULL implies the floor). Relaxed only by changing that decision through the T1 policy, never by violating it.
kind_meaning.soft: Goal with a non-negative deviation variable, minimized at its tier (lexicographic: a lower tier never worsens a higher one).
kind_meaning.objective: A maximize / minimize term at its tier (no target value).
kind_meaning.output: An obligation on what the plan must state (offers, lists, warnings, why). Checked on the plan, costs nothing in the optimization.
kind_meaning.definition: How a quantity is computed (credit, minutes, targets). Not a constraint; every constraint reads it.

how_to_read.metric: metric.compute names fields of the plan/2 JSON (weeks[].weekly_sets_by_group, main_sets_by_group, weekly_sets_by_line, target_by_muscle, step_by_muscle, total_main_sets, total_resistance_sets, athletic_budget, plyo_stage, days[].est_minutes, minutes_limit, kind, blocks[].items[] with sets / credits / bucket / role / group / laterality; plan.time_check; meta.targets; meta.stairway) so a scorer can compute it without engine internals.

tiers.name: Safety and hard rules
tiers.what: Never violated. Safety, eligibility, locked coach rules (rules.locked LK01-LK18), counting definitions, session-structure rules the coach called hard (core first, power before strength, horizontal before vertical, hip+push / knee+pull, two spine days, never 1 exercise for a trained group, one calf exercise per leg day, 12 + 2 for field athletes), the step and weekly-rise limits, test timing, athletic safety. A plan that cannot satisfy T0 is refused (refer) or its offending block is removed - never shipped with a T0 violation.
tiers.coach: GEN-08 "Hard rules it must never break" + locked list; R2-SES-01/02; R2-SES-04; R2-SES-05; R3-SES-01

tiers.name: R3-SES-02 infeasibility policy
tiers.role: which groups are trained directly (and in what state), the offers
tiers.what: Lexicographic maximization of the trained-group state vector in the keep order, subject to T0 and to the minimums of a trained group (floor, 2-4 per trained day, minimum climb) and to "the day holds" (minutes x fit factor). Offers (one more day, longer sessions, block toggles) are always computed and shown first.
tiers.coach: R3-SES-02 (RIGHT): (1) tell up front + offer; (2) train fewer muscles directly, big movers first; (3) supersets; (4) never flat. "Never squeeze 2-4 exercises per muscle into a day that can't hold them."

tiers.name: Floors on trained groups
tiers.role: conditional hard (y_g = FULL) + soft deficit for listed exemptions
tiers.what: Every directly trained FOCUS group holds the floor (10; calves by the leg-day rule) on the main days in every week of a training block.
tiers.coach: R2-VOL-06 "I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle"; R3-VOL-01; R3-SES-01

tiers.name: Stairway monotone climb
tiers.role: conditional hard minimum climb + soft shape
tiers.what: Weekly sets never drop, every trained group climbs at least the minimum climb, no long holds, the last week is the hardest, the early steps are smaller than the late ones, whole sets track the planned T(w). Athletic doses climb with the block and never drop.
tiers.coach: R2-PER-03 (NOT RIGHT -> "steps up a stairway ... that goes for every plan"); R2-PER-04; R3-VOL-04 (RIGHT); R3-SES-02 step 4 "never flat"

tiers.name: Time fit
tiers.role: soft below the "day holds" band of T1
tiers.what: Day minutes within the chosen session length; the x1.10 band is spent only on the minimums (T1-T3), never on extra ceiling height. Only the overrun is minimized here: terms that would reward less volume (fewer supersets, a shorter longest day, fewer exercises) sit below the ceiling attainment of T5.
tiers.coach: UNI-09 "it has to be accounted for"; R2-SES-05 "it might be a little longer day"; R3-SES-02 "they should be able to get things done"

tiers.name: Caps (and ceiling attainment)
tiers.role: upper bounds + the peak height objective
tiers.what: Direct sets never above the line ceiling, never above the absolute 30; per-session and per-exercise limits; then reach as close to the ceiling as the minutes allow in the last week. Athletic budget caps and attainment live here.
tiers.coach: R2-VOL-06 caps 14/22/25, priority 18/26-28/30 ("this is all customizable"); R3-VOL-04 "reaches its ceiling exactly in the last week"; R3-SES-01 Focus +1..+3

tiers.name: Exercise counts
tiers.what: Exercise caps by session length on split days, 3-4 per group preferred on split days, fewest exercises (sets go to existing exercises first), added exercises enter at 2 sets at an exercise-block start, Focus slots 2 x 2-3 sets.
tiers.coach: VOL-08, VOL-16, VOL-07, ORD-11; UNI-09 "Ideally, just do not add too much"

tiers.what: VOL-07 staircase inside a day, R3-VOL-03 alternation between the two exposures of a day type, bonus / Focus placement, default orders, same- vs cross-pattern pairing, superset recommendations and straight sets by default, even exposure days, week shape and frequency.
tiers.coach: VOL-07; R3-VOL-03 (RIGHT); ORD-04; UNI-06; ORD-05; R2-ATH-04

definitions.title: Hard set (the counting unit)
definitions.plain: A working set at 1-3 reps in reserve, 5-30 reps. Warm-up sets and A-drills never count; the light core-opener sets count toward abs.
definitions.formal: hard(set) ⟺ RIR ∈ [1,3] (MAX = 0 RIR allowed only where T0-SAFE-04 allows) ∧ reps ∈ [5,30]; ρ(s) ∈ {warmup} ⇒ n_{s,w} contributes 0 to every V, Q.

definitions.title: Credit map: prime 1.0, helpers 0.25, the coach exceptions
definitions.plain: Main mover 1.0 set, helpers 0.25. Squats / lunges / deadlifts / RDLs give glutes 0.25; hip thrusts and bridges 1.0 glutes; dips 0.5 triceps + 0.5 chest; thruster 1.0 quads + 0.5 front delts + 0.25 glutes; leg curl / leg extension count fully; face pull rear 1.0 + side 0.25 (split PROPOSED); curls 0.25 forearms.

definitions.title: Athletic and ballistic work credits no muscle
definitions.plain: Plyos, ballistics (KB swings included), throws, Olympic lifts, sprints, change of direction, HYROX station circuits, wall balls: 0 muscle sets. Locked (LK07).

definitions.title: Group credit: a set counts at most 1.0 to a line or a group
definitions.plain: Hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts (+ traps). An RDL is one hips set (not 1.25); a face pull one shoulder set; a horizontal press 0.25 shoulders.
definitions.formal: c_l(x) = min(1, Σ_{m ∈ members(l)} c_m(x));  c_g(x) = min(1, Σ_{m ∈ members(g)} c_m(x)).

definitions.title: A 10/10 unilateral set is one set; alternating = unilateral
definitions.plain: 3 x 10/10 split squats = 3 quad sets. Unilateral sets cost about 1.5x the time (DEF-09).
definitions.formal: unilateral or alternating x: n_{s,w} counts once toward c (not per side).

definitions.title: MYO sets do not change set counts
definitions.plain: A MYO set is reported as 2 equivalent sets for display only; it never changes V, Q, caps or floors.
definitions.formal: myo(s,w) ⇒ V, Q unchanged; myo_equivalent_sets reported.

definitions.title: Joint care (prehab) credits no muscle
definitions.plain: Easy face pulls, Y-T raises, soleus / tibialis raises done as joint care are survival work, not hard sets toward the floor.
definitions.formal: ρ(s) = prehab ⇒ c_m(x_s) := 0 for V, Q.

definitions.title: Trained directly / exercises of a group on a day
definitions.plain: A group is trained on a day when a station on that day has it as prime mover (joint care and kept pattern stations excluded). A group left to compound credit, a credit-only line and a kept pattern station are not "trained that day".
definitions.formal: z_{g,d} = [K_{g,d,e} ≥ 1];  y_g = [state_g = FULL];  PATTERN stations and credit_only lines excluded from K and from the floor.

definitions.title: The time model (minutes of a set, a superset, a day)
definitions.plain: A set costs its work time plus the rest it is dosed with. A superset pair works back to back and shares one rest (the longest). A day = warm-up + core + every block, changeovers included.
definitions.formal:
τ(s,w) = work_minutes[tc(s)] + rest_class_minutes[rc(s,w)], tc = time class (unilateral pick → compound_unilateral / isolation_unilateral), rc = strength for heavy work lifts (strength / class family, heavy_powerlifting style, athletes VOL3 bilateral main compound), else by tc.
straight(s) = n_{s,w}·τ(s,w) + co,  co = changeover_min_per_exercise.
superset(P) = Σ_{k=1}^{max_s n_s} [ Σ_{s∈P: n_s ≥ k} work(s) + max_{s∈P: n_s ≥ k} rest(s) ] + co_pair·|P|.
Min_{d,w} = warmup + skill_in_warmup + Σ_straight + Σ_supersets + athletic / Olympic / conditioning / circuit / aerobic add-on minutes + test minutes (work-up 10).

definitions.title: The planned stairway T_l(w)
definitions.plain: CX-01/03: standard 3%/5% weights are a reference shape; accelerate to the intended endpoint when needed, without raising the applicable set ceiling. Root finding and integer allocation remain proposed procedures; the historical parameter snapshot below is not an active bound on lambda.
definitions.formal: For S_l>0 and N>=2: h=ceil(N/2); s_w=0.03 (2<=w<=h), 0.05 (h<w<=N). S_l is the actual credited start; choose a jointly feasible endpoint P_l with S_l<=P_l<=the applicable ceiling. If P_l=S_l, lambda_l=0. Otherwise solve S_l*product(1+lambda_l*s_w)=P_l with lambda_l>=0, including lambda_l>1 when needed. T_l(1)=S_l; T_l(w)=T_l(w-1)*(1+lambda_l*s_w). Continuous reachability is not proof of discrete/time feasibility; numerical procedure and tolerances require verification.

definitions.title: Bilateral share
definitions.plain: Bilateral sets ÷ (bilateral + unilateral sets) in the lower-body knee- and hip-dominant compound slots (leg flexion, leg extension and isolation excluded); the upper body by the same logic (alternating = unilateral).
definitions.formal: β^{lower}_e = Σ_{s: β(s) ∈ {RP_BKD, RP_UKD, RP_BHD, RP_UHD}, bilateral(x_s)} n / Σ_{same slots} n over the weeks of e; β^{upper}_e on {RP_HPUSH, RP_VPUSH, RP_HPULL, RP_VPULL}.

definitions.title: Client level
definitions.plain: L1 = under about a year of consistent training, or 6+ months off (body treated as a beginner); L2 = consistent for over a year; L3 = 3+ years and 4+ days a week, or a competitive physique / strength athlete (PROPOSED). The client level (volume) is separate from the exercise level (difficulty).
definitions.formal: L = L1 if years < 1 ∨ layoff ≥ 6 mo ∨ (former competitor ∧ first block); L3 if years ≥ 3 ∧ days ≥ 4 (inclusive, D-01) ∨ competitive physique / strength; else L2.

derivations.title: Order of operations of a line target
derivations.plain: base → modifier → round half up → Focus add → floor 10 → pain factor → profile ratios → phase factor → cycles → cap ≥ start. Pain wins over the floor.

derivations.title: Calves start and floor from leg days
derivations.plain: One calf exercise x 3 sets every leg day; the weekly floor is the most one exercise a leg day can hold with room for its climb.
derivations.formal: start_calves = 3·n_leg;  F_calves(n_leg) = max(3·n_leg, min(10, 4·n_leg − 1))  (2 leg days → 7, 3 → 10, 4 → 12); timed circuit: 3·n_leg.

derivations.title: Focus muscle 1 and 2
derivations.plain: Up to 2 Focus muscles; each gets +F sets (default 2, range 1-3) on its start and on its ceiling, the ceiling bounded by the priority caps 18 / 26 (chest 28) / 30. v_taper takes both slots (shoulders + back). The other lines are not slowed.
derivations.formal: l ∈ Focus ⇒ S_l += F, C_l = min(C_l + F, prio_cap[l][L]);  |Focus| ≤ 2;  F ∈ [1,3].

derivations.title: Pain declared at intake
derivations.plain: The affected group / pattern starts at 50-70 % (engine 0.6), on constrained machines or split grips, positions that hurt excluded, not floored; a gentle climb (12: ceiling = start + 1; engine: no step in weeks 2-3, then ≤ 3 %).
derivations.formal: l ∈ pain ⇒ S_l = round_half_up(S_l·0.6), l ∉ floored; constraint(x) ∈ [4,5] preferred; share shift 0.2 toward the pain-free side.

derivations.title: One target per FOCUS group outside physique / strength plans
derivations.plain: For field, stay-active, general, fat-loss and in-season clients the hips group carries ONE weekly target (the hamstrings line); glutes follow as credit unless picked as a Focus muscle. Physique and strength plans keep two lines.
derivations.formal: modifier ∈ one_target_groups.modifiers ⇒ hips target on carrier line only; other line fill = credit.

value.status: PROPOSED (F1, E-84): one target per FOCUS group outside physique / strength plans; glutes follow the hamstrings line as credit unless picked as a Focus muscle

derivations.title: Profile volume ratios (swimming)
derivations.plain: Swimmers (and other shoulder-swimmer profiles): back ≥ 1.5 x chest on starts and ceilings.

derivations.title: Next block after completed blocks
derivations.plain: CX-03 holds the applicable set ceiling and continues load/rep progression there. Canonical synthesis section 4 rounds after every completed block, not once after exponentiation. The bounded recurrence is PROPOSED exact implementation; repeat-start and completed-block-count input retain their existing proposed status. Nothing is stored.
derivations.formal: PROPOSED, repeated once per completed block: C_next=min(C_l+1,applicable_cap_l); S_next=min(C_next,round_half_up(1.05*S_l)); (S_l,C_l)=(S_next,C_next). At S_l=C_l: set climb=0 and load/rep progression; never divide by C_l-S_l. Resolve imported S_l>C_l before planning without silently raising the ceiling.

derivations.title: Flat block types (maintenance, pre-season, taper, in-season, recovery)
derivations.plain: Maintenance 50 / 60 / 70 % (vacation or limited kit / travel, moving, season change / planned; older ≥ 70 %) of the last block's final weeks or the level start; pre-season about 60 % of the last off-season week; taper 50 % of pre-season; in-season the athlete_in modifier, 2 days. Flat (step 0), not floored, RIR 2-3.
derivations.formal: type(b) ∈ flat ⇒ n_{s,w} = n_{s,1} ∀w ∈ W_b; sets from the factor; F not applied.

derivations.title: Athletic weekly targets
derivations.plain: Each sport profile gives weekly ranges per key (contacts, throws, cuts, sprint metres, Olympic sets) and tiers; the plyometric share at block end by ground-contact class (75 / 60 / 50 / 40 / 25 %), each block starting 15 points more ballistic; phase factors (pre-season, in-season game-heavy x 0.5, heavy play weeks x 0.5).
derivations.formal: Â_{k,w} = ramp(low_k → high_k over the block) · phase_factor_k;  share*(w) = (end − 0.15) + progress(w)·0.15, counted over jump and throw work.

derivations.title: Aerobic sessions per week

derivations.title: Planned effort by week (the 2 → 11 drift)
derivations.plain: 12 weeks: 3 RIR weeks 1-6, 2 RIR weeks 7-9, 1-2 RIR weeks 10-11, 1 RIR + intensifiers in week 12; display level 2 → 11. Always inside 1-3 RIR.

rules.title: Deterministic, outputs only, computed once
rules.plain: The whole plan is a pure function of the intake and the model, computed once and shown ahead of time; no check-in, tracking or adaptive input changes it; identical inputs give an identical plan. Every tie is broken by a fixed order (rules.muscles.lines.order, session position, weekday order).
rules.formal: plan = Φ(intake, model, seed(intake)); ∀ runs: Φ identical; no clock or randomness except the intake-derived seed; ties broken lexicographically by (line order, pos(s), weekday).

value.note: the generator outputs the whole plan once; people and coaches adjust it themselves; nothing is kept

rules.title: No lifestyle, check-in or tracking inputs; nothing kept
rules.plain: The intake holds no sleep, stress, job or life field and no check-in field; nothing after the build feeds the engine; no data kept.
rules.formal: intake fields ∩ {sleep, stress, job, life, checkin, effort_log} = ∅; no network call with intake / plan data.

metric.compute: fields of the intake / plan.meta.input_audit naming sleep, stress, job, life or check-in

rules.title: Explainable: every dosing decision carries its reason
rules.plain: Every start, ceiling, floor lift, dropped group, cut, offer and placed set carries a why with its source id, and the plan tells the person up front what it could not fit.
rules.formal: ∀ decision δ ∈ {S_l, C̃_l, state_g, cut, offer, n change}: why(δ) ≠ ∅ with ref ∈ sources.
sources: R3-VOL-04 ("the program will tell you to adjust accordingly")

metric.compute: items / week changes / time_check entries without a why ref

rules.title: No sex-based rules
rules.plain: Age, foundation, goal and injuries decide; there is no sex field, and a Focus muscle is the person's choice, never inferred ("if it's a female and she chooses glutes" is an example of a choice).
rules.formal: Φ independent of sex; Focus ⊆ intake.focus_muscles.

metric.compute: intake / plan fields naming sex

rules.title: Health check refers, release before every build
rules.plain: Any health-check refer item (chest pain / heart, surgery or fracture < 6 months, pregnancy / birth < 6 months, injury under treatment, doctor said no) or severe pain: no plan, refer. A coach may bypass with the coach warning. The own-risk + terms + release box is ticked for every build.
rules.formal: refer(intake) ⇒ plan.status = refer ∧ no weeks;  ¬release(intake) ⇒ no plan.

metric.compute: plans with weeks while refer is set or release missing

rules.title: No bands, chains or variable resistance
rules.plain: No exercise, swap or kit token uses a band, chain or weight releaser.
rules.formal: ∀s, e: tags(x_{s,e}) ∩ {band, chain, releaser} = ∅ (swaps included).

metric.compute: items or swaps whose exercise has a band / chain tag

rules.title: No V-squat
rules.plain: The V-squat never appears.
rules.formal: ∀s, e: x_{s,e} ≠ v-squat.

metric.compute: items with a v-squat exercise id

rules.title: Never to failure on heavy compounds; MAX only on small-muscle / bodyweight last sets
rules.plain: Planned effort stays at 1-3 RIR on every working set; MAX (technical failure) only as the last set of a small-muscle or bodyweight item.
rules.formal: RIR(s,w) ∈ [1,3] ∀ heavy compound s;  MAX(s,w) ⇒ class(x_s) ∈ {small_muscle_isolation, rear_delts, calves} ∨ bodyweight(x_s), last set only.

metric.compute: compound items with effort.min < 1 or a MAX last set

rules.title: Older adults (60+): the never list and the opt-in power work
rules.plain: Overhead and low-bar squats never. By default off: plyometric jumps, ankle hops, Olympic lifts, ballistic jumps (switchable on with the warning "Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means"). Depth jumps, high depth drops and snatches stay locked even with the opt-in (Phase 0 strict reading). On by default: landing drills, balance, quick stepping without a hop, light medball throws, fast machine work. Constrained machines preferred.
rules.formal: age ≥ 60 ⇒ ∀s: tags(x_s) ∩ (never_tags ∪ never_tags_phase0_even_with_opt_in) = ∅ ∧ (¬opt_in ⇒ quality(x_s) ∉ default_excluded_qualities).

metric.compute: items for a 60+ client with a never tag, or default-off quality without prefs opt-in

rules.title: Racket players 50+ and pickleball / padel / tennis defaults
rules.plain: Knee-friendly strength; calf and Achilles work every leg day; rotator-cuff and elbow care weekly (kept on a main day, never cut for time); only low-impact jumps (no depth jumps, high drops, hurdle hops or bounds) unless switched on.
rules.formal: age ≥ 50 ∧ profile ∈ racket ⇒ ∀d ∈ D^leg: ∃ prehab_lower(d); ∃ arm-care station on some d ∈ D^main per week; tags(x) ∩ {depth_jump, high_depth_drop, hurdle_hop, bound} = ∅ unless opt-in.

metric.compute: leg days of a racket 50+ client without lower prehab + weeks without arm care on a main day + avoided-tag items

rules.title: Youth limits
rules.plain: Under 18: exercise ladder up to intermediate; Olympic lifts from the floor only from about 14 and after one block of hang work; medballs 2 lb lighter; guardian release.
rules.formal: age < 18 ⇒ ladder(x) ≤ intermediate; floor_olympic(x) ⇒ age ≥ 14 ∧ previous_cycles ≥ 1.

metric.compute: youth items above the ladder or floor Olympic lifts before the rule allows

rules.title: Pain areas: avoid tags, axial limit, refer when severe
rules.plain: Each declared pain area removes the exercises with its avoid tags (e.g. lower back: no good mornings, bent-over, axial-high or counted spine lifts; knee: no deep knee flexion, depth jumps, hurdle hops, bounds), prefers machines / split grips (constraint 4-5), and severe pain refers.
rules.formal: ∀ area a ∈ pain: ∀s: tags(x_s) ∩ avoid(a) = ∅ ∧ axial_class(x_s) ≤ max_axial_class(a);  severity(a) = severe ⇒ refer.

metric.compute: items whose exercise carries an avoid tag of a declared pain area

rules.title: Medball ≤ 20 lb; no medball in the aesthetics main workout
rules.plain: Medballs never over 20 lb (light 8-10 lb for passes, 6-10 overhead, 10-20 slams); aesthetics / bodybuilders use the medball only in the warm-up.
rules.formal: load_lb(x_s) ≤ 20 ∀ medball s;  goal = muscle ⇒ no medball item outside the warm-up.

metric.compute: medball items > 20 lb or an aesthetics main-workout medball item

rules.title: Equipment availability
rules.plain: Every pick is doable with the client's kit (access profile + extra items + machines owned); no-ball substitutes only when no medball is owned.
rules.formal: ∀s, e: x_{s,e} ∈ X_s(kit).

metric.compute: items whose exercise needs equipment outside the kit

rules.title: Library exercises only; one-detail variations; never invented
rules.plain: The library is the single source of truth; between exercise blocks the tool may change one detail (hand, grip, stance, implement, range) and show it as "<name> - <detail>"; it never invents an exercise; swap-only / generic records are never the pick.
rules.formal: ∀s, e: x_{s,e} ∈ X^live ∪ {(x, detail): x ∈ X^live, detail ∈ variations(x)}; status(x) ∉ swap_only_statuses.

value.status: one-detail rule COACH-R2 R2-LIB-01 / COACH-ANSWER PER-02; distance scoring and vocabulary PROPOSED (B3)

metric.compute: items whose exercise id is not in the catalog (live) or carries a non-library detail

rules.title: Slot-type exclusions (KB swings, Olympic catches)
rules.plain: KB swings (and wall balls) never fill a resistance slot (they are ballistic, power block or WOD only); a jerk / Olympic catch never fills a resistance, isolation or Focus slot; a push press presses only for athletes and class-model clients.
rules.formal: κ(s) ∈ {strength, accessories, focus} ⇒ tags(x_s) ∩ {kb_swing, wall_ball, olympic_catch} = ∅.

metric.compute: resistance / isolation / focus items with a kb_swing, wall_ball or Olympic catch exercise

rules.title: No max test from zero
rules.plain: Someone untrained, back from a layoff, under a year of training or a minor never tests a 1RM or a max-effort mile: 5-8RM (L1) / 3-5RM and 80-90 % efforts instead.
rules.formal: from_zero(intake) ⇒ test kind ∈ {rm_5_8, rm_3_or_5, submax_80_90}.

metric.compute: test items with 1RM / max mile for a from-zero client

rules.title: Warm-up every session; drills never volume
rules.plain: Every session opens with a warm-up (5 min any cardio + A-drills on lower / athletic days or mobility on press days); A-drills never count.
rules.formal: ∀d ∈ D^main: first block κ = warmup;  c(warmup items) = 0.

metric.compute: main days whose first block is not warmup

rules.title: Core opener: 2 exercises x 2 sets, short of failure, first
rules.plain: Right after the warm-up every main session has the core block: 2 exercises x 2 sets, short of failure (RIR ≥ 2), one thorax + one pelvis. The person may move it (after plyos / after strength / end) or switch it off for a day; the generator never leaves it out.
rules.formal: ∀d ∈ D^main: |core items| = 2 ∧ n = 2 ∧ RIR ≥ 2 ∧ pos(core) = start unless prefs.core_position; generator: toggle = on.

metric.compute: main days without a 2 x 2 core block in its position

rules.title: Block order
rules.plain: warm-up → core → test → skill → athletic → power (Olympic) → strength → accessories → joint care → circuit → conditioning → aerobic → cool-down, except the allowed overrides (contrast station, a priority small muscle first, core moved by the person, the bootcamp cardio station, a fighter's opening aerobic block, the vertical work lift first).
rules.formal: ∀d: blocks of d appear as a subsequence of block_order, up to allowed_overrides.

metric.compute: days whose block kinds break ordering.block_order without an allowed override

rules.title: Power before strength
rules.plain: Every athletic / Olympic item comes before every strength item of the day (contrast complexes excepted).
rules.formal: ∀d: max pos(athletic ∪ power) < min pos(strength ∪ accessories), contrast excepted.

metric.compute: days with an athletic / power item after a strength item

rules.title: Horizontal before vertical (row before pulldown, flat before overhead)
rules.plain: Within a day every horizontal pull precedes every vertical pull and every horizontal push precedes every vertical push - except when the vertical lift is the day's work lift ("the work first").
rules.formal: ∀d: pos(HPULL) < pos(VPULL) ∧ pos(HPUSH) < pos(VPUSH), unless ρ(vertical) = work.

metric.compute: days with a vertical pull / push before a horizontal one (non-work vertical)

rules.title: The work first; bilateral before unilateral; MYO last
rules.plain: On days holding a work lift, the work comes first in the strength block, and bilateral lifts precede unilateral ones of the same region (machine MYO finisher exempt); MYO only on the day's last eligible item.
rules.formal: ∃ work on d ⇒ pos(work) = min pos(strength); pos(bilateral_reg) < pos(unilateral_reg); MYO(s) ⇒ s = last eligible item of d.

metric.compute: days breaking work-first, bilateral-before-unilateral or MYO-last

rules.title: Athletic order and the speed session order
rules.plain: Sprint → plyo → ankle work → throws → COD inside the athletic block, all before Olympic work; speed sessions: squirrel jumps → MACH / acceleration starts → max velocity.
rules.formal: pos follows athletic_bucket_order; athletic < power; speed order fixed.

metric.compute: days breaking the athletic bucket order or speed order

rules.title: Hip-dominant + push, knee-dominant + pull
rules.plain: In every session mixing lower and upper work (full body, bootcamp, athletic), the hip-dominant lower lift pairs with a push and the knee-dominant one with a pull (upper/lower and PPL variants excepted).
rules.formal: ∀d mixed, ∀ lower work / secondary s: β(s) ∈ hip_buckets ⇒ partner(s) ∈ hip_with; β(s) ∈ knee_buckets ⇒ partner(s) ∈ knee_with.

metric.compute: mixed days whose lower lift is paired with the wrong upper vector

rules.title: Two spine days: heavy squat and heavy deadlift on different days, once each per week
rules.plain: At most one counted (axial) squat day and one counted hinge day a week, never on the same day. Counted: barbell back, front, zercher, overhead and Smith squats; barbell or trap-bar deadlifts and RDLs; good mornings. Not counted: leg press, belt squat, hip thrust, back extension, reverse hyper, single-leg DB work, Olympic lifts, loaded jumps. Goblet / hack / pendulum fine on the second day if not sore; powerlifters may add a light technique squat or deadlift.
rules.formal: Σ_d [∃s ∈ S_d: counted_squat(x_s)] ≤ 1;  Σ_d [∃s ∈ S_d: counted_hinge(x_s)] ≤ 1;  ¬∃d with both.

metric.compute: weeks with > 1 counted squat day, > 1 counted hinge day, or both on one day

rules.title: Never 1 exercise for a trained group on a day (2-4)
rules.plain: Every FOCUS group trained on a day gets 2 to 4 exercises that day, split and full-body days alike ("there's never one exercise"). A group that cannot get 2 on a day leaves that day. Exempt: calves (exactly 1), the core opener (2), conjugate four-role strength days (as written), timed circuit days, a class-model work lift kept alone.
rules.formal: ∀ g ∉ {calves, core}, ∀d, e: K_{g,d,e} ∈ {0} ∪ [2, 4], except exempt families / circuit days / class lift.

metric.compute: (stairway week, main day, g ∈ time_check.trained_groups \ {calves}) with weeks[].group_counts_by_day[weekday][g] = 1, or > 4; circuit days and the class-model work lift exempt

rules.title: Calves: one calf exercise on every leg day, at least 3 sets
rules.plain: When calves are trained, every leg day holds exactly one calf exercise (never a second calf exercise on a leg day), 3+ sets; extra calf sets go to that exercise (≤ 4) or the optional-day Calves slot.
rules.formal: state_calves = FULL ⇒ ∀d ∈ D^leg: #{s ∈ S_d: β(s) = ISO_CALF} = 1 ∧ n ≥ 3;  ∀d: #{ISO_CALF} ≤ 1.

metric.compute: leg days of a calves-trained plan without exactly one calf exercise at ≥ 3 sets, or any day with 2 calf exercises

rules.title: A rear-delt exercise every week while the shoulders are trained
rules.plain: Rear delts are not an individual muscle, but every plan keeps rear-delt work each week: a rear-delt station, or rows giving ≥ 1.5 rear-delt credit sets; the person can always add more.
rules.formal: state_shoulders = FULL ⇒ (∃s: β(s) ∈ {ISO_REAR, FACEPULL}) ∨ Σ_{s: HPULL} n_{s,w}·0.25 ≥ 1.5.

metric.compute: weeks with shoulders trained and no rear station and < 1.5 row rear credit

rules.title: Field athletes: 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block
rules.plain: Off-season field athletes: at most 12 counted exercises a day, the core block, warm-up, skill, joint care, conditioning, aerobic and cool-down outside the count; a superset of two small isolations counts as one; the low ankle block is outside the count.
rules.formal: ∀d ∈ D^main: #{s ∈ S_d counted} ≤ 12, counted = κ ∉ outside_cap_blocks, small-iso pair = 1.

metric.compute: field-athlete days with > 12 counted exercises

rules.title: Exercises fixed inside an exercise block (4-6 weeks)
rules.plain: Inside an exercise block only sets, reps, load and RIR change; exercises change only at an exercise-block start.
rules.formal: ∀s, ∀w, w′ ∈ e: x_{s,w} = x_{s,w′} ∧ u_{s,w} = u_{s,w′} (an added bonus / Focus exercise opens only at an exercise-block start, T6-CNT-04).

metric.compute: exercise ids (or details) that change between weeks of one exercise block

rules.title: Sets per exercise: 2 to 4 (L1) / 5 (L2-L3), isolation ≤ 4
rules.plain: Every working exercise holds at least 2 sets (an added exercise enters at 2) and at most 4 (L1) or 5 (L2-L3); isolation at most 4; calves ≤ 4 per leg day.
rules.formal: 2 ≤ n_{s,w} ≤ max_sets[L] (iso: 4) for resistance s with u = 1; recovery weeks ≥ 1.

metric.compute: resistance items with sets outside [2, max] (stairway weeks)

rules.title: Superset legality
rules.plain: Never two lower-body compounds; never a heavy lift with a fatiguing lift for the same muscle (contrast complexes excepted); pairs from the recommendation list; light weeks drop supersets except small-isolation pairs.
rules.formal: p_{s,s′} = 1 ⇒ ¬(lower_compound(s) ∧ lower_compound(s′)) ∧ prime(s) ∩ prime(s′) = ∅ (contrast excepted) ∧ {class(s), class(s′)} ∈ pairs.

metric.compute: superset pairs of two lower compounds or one muscle twice (non-contrast)

rules.title: Day spacing around play and games; an OFF day
rules.plain: The hardest gym day sits at least 48 h before the biggest play day (stay-active) or the game (in-season); optional, WOD-only and aerobic days go on free weekdays nearest the template day, skipping play and game days; at least one full OFF day.
rules.formal: gap_h(hardest(D^main), biggest(D^play)) ≥ 48; D^opt ∩ D^play = ∅; |OFF| ≥ 1.

metric.compute: weeks breaking the 48-h rule, optional days on play days, or no OFF day

rules.title: Planned effort inside 1-3 RIR, drifting 3 → 1 RIR, never rising
rules.plain: Planned RIR follows the stairway level (DER-13) inside the 1-3 band; it never rises week over week in a stairway; flat blocks RIR 2-3; recovery ≥ 3.
rules.formal: RIR_w ∈ [1,3]; RIR_{w+1} ≤ RIR_w in a stairway; type(b) flat ⇒ RIR ∈ by_block_type[type].

metric.compute: weeks with planned RIR outside the band or rising inside a stairway

rules.title: Intensifiers: last stairway week only, one a day, MYO on the last eligible item
rules.plain: Only in the last stairway week; at most one per training day; a MYO set on the day's last small-muscle or machine-isolation item; never on a free-weight compound, a glute bridge / thrust, or calves of an Achilles hot spot.
rules.formal: intensifier(s,w) ⇒ w = N ∧ s = last eligible item of d ∧ class(x_s) ∉ never_credit_classes; Σ_{s∈S_d} intensifier ≤ 1.

value.eligible: last small-muscle (side / rear delts, biceps, triceps, calves) or machine isolation exercise of the day
value.status: COACH-R3 R3-VOL-04 (last week); one per day PROPOSED

metric.compute: intensifier items outside the last week, > 1 per day, or on an ineligible item

rules.title: Rest by class (VOL-14) - the input of every minute estimate
rules.plain: Hypertrophy 1-2 min (up to 3), isolation 60-90 s, strength 3-6 min (work lifts of strength / class plans, heavy powerlifting style, athletes' VOL3 main compounds, tests), Olympic 2-3 min, core 30-60 s; supersets rest after the pair, with numbers.
rules.formal: rest(s,w) ∈ rest[rc(s,w)]; rc as in DEF-09.

value.after_pair_status: PROPOSED (F3, E-118): each item's own class rest; the pair rests the longest

metric.compute: items whose rest is outside their class range

rules.title: Lift-style preference moves reps, never weekly sets
rules.plain: "Lighter, more reps" vs "heavier, fewer reps" moves the rep range on the big compound lifts only; weekly sets stay the same; small muscles stay high-rep. (It changes rest classes and therefore minutes.)
rules.formal: ∂V_{l,w} / ∂lift_style = 0 for fixed time feasibility; r_{s,w} for big compounds from the preference column.

metric.compute: same intake with two lift styles gives different V targets (time limits equal)

rules.title: Olympic doses: the ramp, full catches 3-5 reps, % only when tested
rules.plain: DB / KB and pull variants keep 4x8 @75 % → 4x6 @80 → 4x6 @85 → 4x4 @90; full squat cleans / snatches (and barbell power catches) 3-5 reps a set with the same weekly reps; RPE / RIR unless the lift's own max was tested.
rules.formal: rep_scheme(x) per olympic.rep_scheme; pct shown ⇔ tested(x).

metric.compute: Olympic items outside their rep scheme or with % untested

rules.title: Strength roles: the work, the accessory, the nuance, the survival
rules.plain: In strength plans (and wherever the roles are used) the work is the main lift at 1 RIR, the accessory a supporting lift at 2 RIR, the nuance weak-point / unilateral / variation work, the survival isolation or joint-health work done no matter what (never cut for time).
rules.formal: ρ(s) = work ⇒ RIR_target 1 (inside the weekly drift band); accessory 2; survival ∈ never_cut.

metric.compute: strength-family days missing their survival item

rules.title: Rep phases and the rep matrix (they set the rest, therefore the minutes)
rules.plain: Athletes run VOL 1 / VOL 2 / VOL 3 one per off-season exercise block (compounds 12-15 → 8-12 → 6-8; pre- and in-season VOL3); big muscles 5-15 mixed, small muscles 12-30; unilateral lifts moderate-high reps; 40-rep sets only inside HYROX / AMRAP circuits. A VOL3 bilateral main compound takes strength rest (3-6 min), which the time model must price at the peak week (E-82, E-125).
rules.formal: r_{s,w} = reps.matrix[class(x_s)][goal column] (athletes: athlete_vol_phases[e]); rc(s,w) = strength when VOL3 ∧ ρ(s) = work ∧ bilateral main compound.

off_late_single_block_step.status: PROPOSED (F3, E-125): built, switched off - open question for the coach (minutes vs groups)

metric.compute: athlete items whose rep bracket does not match the exercise block's VOL phase

rules.title: No deload or maintenance week inside a training block
rules.plain: A block is completed; the easy week (about half of the hardest week, 3+ RIR, no buy-out / finisher / MYO / supersets) sits only between blocks and is a recommendation; a holiday mark inside a block ends that block there.
rules.formal: ∀b stairway, ∀w ∈ W_b: type(week w) = stairway; recovery blocks only between blocks.

metric.compute: weeks of a stairway block flagged deload / maintenance / recovery

rules.title: Planned step ≤ 7 % a week per line
rules.plain: Never more than 7 % a week planned; a hand-set step runs 0-7 % (10 % is never offered).

metric.compute: line-weeks with target_by_muscle step > 7 %

rules.title: Weekly total resistance sets rise below 10 % (one whole set excepted)
rules.plain: "It can progress week by week by 10 %. That's way too much." The person's weekly total rises strictly below 10 %; one whole set may always be added (a small plan can still climb). Placed rule (PROPOSED): a line rises at most max(1 set, 7 %) a week (helpers + 0.5); the week total at most 7 %. Exempt: the first week after a recovery / maintenance phase, block-boundary swaps that add no sets.

value.note: a muscle rises at most max(1 set, 7 %) a week (whole sets, helpers may add 0.5); the week total at most 7 %; 10 % is never reached

metric.compute: weeks whose total_resistance_sets rise ≥ 10 % and > 1 set

rules.title: Flat blocks have no steps; week 1 has no step
rules.plain: Maintenance, pre-season, taper, in-season, recovery and the flat-sets Q1 of the year plan hold their sets; no step in week 1 of any block.
rules.formal: type(b) ∈ flat ⇒ n_{s,w} = n_{s,1}; step_l(1) = 0.

metric.compute: step_by_muscle ≠ 0 in a flat block or week 1

rules.title: Calendar: holidays between blocks, event and meet tapers, pre-season
rules.plain: Marked holidays / vacations sit between blocks (a mark inside a block ends it there); a stay-active event: the hardest weeks end 1 week before, then 1 easy week at about half the sets; swimmers: a 2-week dryland taper before the main championship (1 or none before smaller meets); pre-season 4-6 weeks at about 60 % then a 1-2-week taper; tests in week 1 and the last week only.
rules.formal: block layout from (start, season / event / meet dates, holidays) per plan_types.season / prep; no block straddles a holiday.

metric.compute: blocks straddling a marked holiday or event lead-ins off the rule

rules.title: Tests only at the start and the end; the test is the top set
rules.plain: Tests in week 1 (baseline) and the last week of each stairway block, never mid-block, never in pre-season / in-season / taper / recovery / maintenance. A strength test is that week's top set (work up to one top set, the rest back-off sets a step easier); the tested lift takes no stairway step that week; rep-max tests sit only on bilateral compound picks; a hinge test takes a canonical deadlift.
rules.formal: test(s,w) ⇒ w ∈ {1, N_b} ∧ type(b) = stairway; strength test replaces one planned set of s; x_s bilateral compound.

value.status: PROPOSED (F1, E-91): the back-off dose (planned RIR + 1, at least 2)

metric.compute: tests outside week 1 / last week, on non-bilateral picks, or added on top of the planned sets

rules.title: Olympic lifts in every athletic week, level-matched, ≤ 4 exposures
rules.plain: Everyone in athletic training gets Olympic work every week: beginners DB / KB snatches, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls / cleans; L2+ the full scope within the sport's ceiling; up to 4 exposures a week; clean family on knee days, snatch family on hip days (the template station decides); 60+ only by opt-in (no snatch); 2-3 days for swimmers; in-season 2 x 3 once a week, dropped in heavy game weeks.
rules.formal: family = athletic ∧ ¬(age ≥ 60 ∧ ¬opt_in) ⇒ ∀w (except heavy game weeks in season): 1 ≤ #olympic exposures ≤ 4 (swimmers 2-3; in-season 1 x 2x3); tier(x) ≤ olympic.tiers[L]; x within the sport ceiling (power / pull) unless opted in.

metric.compute: athletic weeks without a fillable Olympic item, > 4 exposures, or above the level / sport ceiling

rules.title: Receive-Create stages aligned to exercise blocks, never backwards
rules.plain: 1 Land → 2 Land & Go → 3 Repeat (12 weeks: 1-3 / 4-7 / 8-12; 8 weeks: 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8), snapped to exercise blocks (each block takes the stage most of its weeks have, ties lower, one stage at a time); never back down inside a training block; restart at stage 1 each off-season; hold in maintenance / pre-season; L2-L3 may start at stage 2; stage qualities: RC1 landing + ballistic, RC2 + plyometric, RC3 ballistic + plyometric (repeat drills).
rules.formal: stage(w) constant on each e; stage(e+1) − stage(e) ∈ {0, 1}; quality(x_s) ∈ stage_qualities[stage(e(w))].

value.status: INFERRED (B2): the approved stage weeks snapped to the exercise blocks

metric.compute: weeks where plyo_stage changes inside an exercise block, goes down, or holds a quality outside its stage

rules.title: Contacts per session and plyo spacing
rules.plain: Plyometric contacts per session ≤ 80 (L1) / 100 (L2) / 120 (L3); 2-3 plyo sessions a week off-season, 48-72 h apart for the same area (masters 3-4 days); depth jumps ≤ 2 stations a week (1 for athletes ≥ 220 lb or L1); the first reactive block bilateral, unloaded, low box; loaded jumps 10-20 % body weight.
rules.formal: Σ_{s ∈ S_d} contacts(s,w) ≤ cap[L]; gap(plyo days, same area) ≥ 48 h; #depth_jump stations ≤ 2 (1).

metric.compute: days over the contacts cap or plyo days closer than the gap

rules.title: In-season game-heavy and heavy play weeks
rules.plain: Game-heavy sports in season (basketball, volleyball, soccer, football, hockey, lacrosse, field hockey, rugby, ultimate, flag football, beach volleyball): gym plyos about half, no extra COD, sprints only for speed athletes, Olympic 2 x 3 once a week, the hard gym day ≥ 48 h before a game. Stay-active weeks with 3+ play sessions drop the extra agility drills and half the jumps.
rules.formal: in_season ∧ game_heavy ⇒ Â_plyo ×= 0.5, Â_cod_extra = 0, olympic = 2x3 x1;  play_sessions ≥ 3 ⇒ Â_jumps ×= 0.5, extra COD = 0.

metric.compute: in-season / heavy-play weeks over the reduced targets

rules.title: Sport defaults the coach approved (swimming, HYROX)
rules.plain: Swimmers: shoulder care (external rotation, floor Y/T raises, KB face pulls) every session, never bands, never cut for time; 0 extra gym cardio; 25 % plyo share at block end; Olympic 2-3 days. HYROX: 2 strength days (squat + pull, deadlift + push) + 2 hybrid days, 4 cardio sessions, 2 short station circuits a week as finishers that never count as muscle sets, wall balls ≤ 20 lb, 40-rep / AMRAP sets only inside them, 50 % plyo share.
rules.formal: profile = swimming ⇒ ∀d ∈ D^main: ∃ shoulder-care station; profile = hyrox ⇒ station circuits κ = conditioning, c = 0.

value.status: approved (R3-ATH-03); station list order and finisher dose PROPOSED

metric.compute: swimmer main days without shoulder care; HYROX circuits credited as muscle sets

rules.title: The minimums of a directly trained group
rules.plain: A group counts as trained directly (state FULL) only if, in every week of the stairway block: (a) it holds its floor on the main days (10; calves by DER-04), (b) it gets 2-4 exercises on every day it is trained (calves 1), (c) it climbs at least the minimum climb by the last week and never drops.

value.status: PROPOSED (2-set climb; 1 set in blocks of 7 weeks or less)

metric.compute: trained groups (time_check.trained_groups) failing floor, 2-4 or climb

rules.title: "The day holds": minutes within the fit factor, with every eligible pair supersetted, at the peak week
rules.plain: A day holds the plan when its minutes - with every eligible pair supersetted - stay within the chosen length x 1.10 ("a little longer day") in every week, the peak week included. A set placed in week 1 must also fit the peak week's costs (its Olympic sets, the VOL3 strength rest).
rules.formal: ∀d ∈ D^main, ∀w: Min^{ss}_{d,w} ≤ φ·μ_d,  φ = fit_factor (full-body days), split days φ_split; Min^{ss} = Min with p = 1 on every legal pair.

metric.compute: non-test main days with est_minutes > fit_factor x minutes_limit

rules.title: Step 0: the full level plan when it fits
rules.plain: Build the level plan (every template group at its level start and ceiling) inside the chosen days x minutes; if every trained group meets its minimums and every line reaches its planned peak, output it with no warning.
rules.formal: if ∃ feasible plan with state_g = FULL ∀g ∈ G* (G* = template groups minus credit-only) and C̃_l = C_l ∀l: choose it.

metric.compute: a plan whose full level plan fits carries no time warning

rules.title: Step 1: tell up front and offer (before the plan)
rules.plain: When the full plan does not fit: say so before week 1 with the numbers, and offer (A) one more day - the next template up, checked the same way; (B) longer sessions - the full plan's peak-week need with supersets, rounded up to 5 min, within the allowed lengths; (C) the block toggles that save time (core / athletic off on some days) with the minutes saved. PROPOSED addition (open, E-134): the smallest session length that adds each next group in keep order.
rules.formal: ¬fits(G*) ⇒ O ⊇ {more_days(d+1, fit check), longer(⌈m*/5⌉·5), toggles(block, Δmin)}, m* = min{μ ∈ minutes_allowed: fits(G*, μ)}; rendered before week 1.

metric.compute: plans with time_check.fits = false and no offers (or offers after week 1)

rules.title: Step 2: keep the time - train fewer groups directly, in the keep order
rules.plain: If the person keeps their time, choose which groups are trained directly by priority: Focus groups and the groups the sport pins first, then the big movers (hips, quads, back, chest), then shoulders, calves, triceps, biceps. A group is kept only if every kept group still meets its minimums (T1-POL-01) and every day holds (T1-POL-02). Never drop every group below the floor instead.
rules.formal: lex-max (state_{π_1}, state_{π_2}, …, state_{π_n}) over the feasible set (T0 ∧ T1-POL-01 ∧ T1-POL-02), π = keep order; equivalently max Σ_i 4^{n−i}·state_{π_i}.  π = Focus groups ⊕ profile-pinned groups (racket 50+: calves) ⊕ profile big priorities ⊕ keep_order (athletic families: keep_order_r2.athletic) with duplicates removed.
sources: R3-SES-02 step 2 ("big movers first; arms, calves and rear delts only from compound credit")

metric.compute: groups kept FULL while an earlier group in π is not FULL although adding it (and dropping the later one) is feasible - measured against an exhaustive check

rules.title: Room cuts before groups: what leaves the day first
rules.plain: Before any group loses its FULL state, non-group room goes, in the family's cut order (aesthetics: Focus slot, second calf, duplicate isolation, aquatic chest fly, third exercise of a group, second non-axial bilateral; athletic: Olympic over budget, second plyo / sprint, second jump for low-contact sports, COD for non-COD sports, buy-out, second throw, ...; stay-active: Olympic over budget, joint care to the optional day, ankle block, one athletic station a day, second jump, second throw, COD, buy-out, ...). Never cut: the core block, the work lift and its paired upper lift, survival work, the first calf station, the week's last rear-delt station, a group below 2 exercises, the last plyo / ballistic station of an athlete. Supersets are tried first.
rules.formal: cuts c ∈ cut_order[family] applied in order while ¬fits; c never removes never_cut items; a cut is kept only if it raises the lex value of T1-POL-05.

value.status: PROPOSED (v1.2 review: Olympic sets above the budget, 1-set fillers and duplicate isolations go before any target muscle)
value.group_moves: retired (v1.3): the time check (R3-SES-02) decides which groups are trained directly

metric.compute: never_cut items missing from a day that holds its group

rules.title: Pattern coverage: big movers not trained directly keep their movement (anti over-cut)
rules.plain: Every primary pattern stays in the week: a big mover the time leaves untrained directly keeps one pattern station (back: horizontal row, chest: horizontal press, quads: single-leg knee, hips: single-leg hinge), 2 sets, paired with the day's work lift, not counted toward the floor, at most 3 a week. This is the rule the "pickleball plan with only hinges" broke; the coach's step 2 ("arms, calves and rear delts only from compound credit") presumes the presses and rows stay.
rules.formal: ∀g ∈ {back, chest, quads, hips}: state_g ∈ {FULL, BELOW_FLOOR, PATTERN} whenever a PATTERN station fits (state PATTERN = 1 station, n = 2, c excluded from the floor); Σ PATTERN stations ≤ 3.

value.status: PROPOSED (F1, E-94): pattern stations on the optional day for the big movers the minutes leave untrained directly

metric.compute: weeks without a knee, hip, horizontal push and horizontal pull station (main + optional days)

rules.title: Relaxed states: a big mover below its floor on its work lift; the class lift
rules.plain: A big mover that cannot hold 10 sets but can hold the day's work lift may be kept below its floor, still climbing (state BELOW_FLOOR), listed "trained below the floor (time)"; in the CrossFit class model a group not trained directly keeps its class lift (3 sets, heavier by the week). Tried after the groups that hold their floor and only if no kept big mover loses its floor or climb.
rules.formal: state_g = BELOW_FLOOR ⇒ ∃ work lift of g; Q_{g,N} − Q_{g,1} ≥ mc_calves; listed in trained_below_floor; lex rank FULL > BELOW_FLOOR > PATTERN > NONE.

value.status: PROPOSED (B4, E-64): the coach approved fewer groups trained directly (R3-SES-02, his CrossFit-class example); keeping the class lift of a group not trained directly is PROPOSED

metric.compute: groups under the floor not listed in time_check.trained_below_floor / not_trained_directly

rules.title: Never squeeze: a group leaves a day rather than taking 1 exercise
rules.plain: Never squeeze 2-4 exercises per group into a day that cannot hold them: the group trains on its other days with 2+ exercises each; a lone station whose partner found no pick leaves the day; calves stay on every leg day or leave the plan.
rules.formal: if K_{g,d} = 2 does not fit on d ⇒ z_{g,d} = 0 (never K_{g,d} = 1).

metric.compute: same as T0-SES-10 (1-exercise groups)

rules.title: Groups not trained directly are listed honestly, with their compound credit
rules.plain: A group left out keeps its compound credit (rows → biceps and rear delts, presses → triceps and front delts, squats / hinges → glutes) and is listed "not trained directly (time)"; a group the plan gives no credited set at all is printed "not trained in this plan because of time" with the offer.
rules.formal: ∀g: state_g ≠ FULL ⇒ g ∈ NT with reason ∈ {time, credit_only, no_station, class_lift} and its credited Q_{g,w} shown.

metric.compute: template groups neither trained nor in time_check.not_trained_directly

rules.title: Step 3: supersets recommended, "needed" when the fit depends on them
rules.plain: Every eligible pair of every day carries a superset recommendation with the minutes it saves; when a day only fits with it, it is marked needed and switched on ("Recommend doing supersets so that it's a faster workout").
rules.formal: ∀ legal (s,s′): rec_{s,s′} = 1 with Δmin; fits(d) depends on p ⇒ p_{s,s′} = 1 ∧ needed.

metric.compute: days with eligible pairs but no superset_recommendations entry; needed pairs not on

rules.title: Step 4: the stairway climbs on every trained group, to the ceiling the time holds
rules.plain: Each trained line climbs from its week-1 sets to the ceiling its time holds (λ re-solved so it lands there in the last week), never below week 1 + the minimum climb; the keep-time ceiling is clamped to the level ceiling.
rules.formal: state_g ∈ {FULL, BELOW_FLOOR} ⇒ C̃_l = min(C_l, P^time_l) with C̃_l ≥ S_l + mc; λ_l solves DEF-10 with C̃_l.

value.status: PROPOSED (2-set climb; 1 set in blocks of 7 weeks or less)

metric.compute: trained groups with last-week minus week-1 below the minimum climb

rules.title: Athletic blocks inside the policy: protected for competitive athletes, room for stay-active
rules.plain: Competitive athletes keep the sport's tracks (the R3-SES-01 split: 2 jump / throw stations + 1 Olympic lift on a cross-pattern day) - their tracks are not time-cut; stay-active and general clients give up athletic room first (one athletic station a day, the power block switched off, switchable back on) before any big mover leaves.
rules.formal: competitive ⇒ athletic tracks ∈ never_cut (inside the 12 + 2 split); stay-active ⇒ athletic room cuts precede any state_g decrease for g ∈ big movers.
sources: R3-SES-02 ("turn off that day's athletic training ... focus on resistance")

metric.compute: stay-active plans where a big mover is not trained while an athletic room cut was available

rules.title: User edits are constraints on a rebuild; the person's choice wins
rules.plain: Switching off a day's athletic / core / accessory / cardio block, removing or adding an exercise or a block rebuilds the same plan with the edit as a constraint; edits produce notes, never refusals; athletic, Olympic, core and conditioning blocks never count as muscle sets, so switching them off changes no stairway; "add rear delts" is always offered.
rules.formal: plan(edits) = Φ(intake ∪ edits); edits are fixed u / toggle values; notes when a group falls below its floor or 2-4.

value.id_format_status: PROPOSED (F1, E-90): lower-case weekday + day-type slug (a-z, 0-9, -)

metric.compute: a toggle-off of an athletic / core block leaves weekly_sets_by_group unchanged

rules.title: Floor of 10 weekly sets on every directly trained FOCUS group
rules.plain: "Nobody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle": every directly trained group - quads, hips, chest, back, shoulders, biceps, triceps (calves by T2-FLR-02) - holds 10+ sets with group credit on the main days, every week of a training block.
rules.formal: ∀g: state_g = FULL, ∀w ∈ W_b (type(b) = stairway): Q^main_{g,w} ≥ F;  F = 10.

metric.compute: Σ over stairway weeks and FULL groups (time_check.trained_groups minus time_check.trained_below_floor) of [main_sets_by_group[g] < 10 − 1e-9] (calves: < meta.targets.calves_floor); below-floor groups are measured by T2-FLR-05

rules.title: Calves floor from leg days
rules.plain: Calves: one exercise x 3 sets every leg day, weekly floor max(3 x leg days, min(10, 4 x leg days − 1)); 10 a week with fewer than 4 leg days needs a 4th set or the optional-day Calves slot (PROPOSED).
rules.formal: state_calves = FULL ⇒ Q_{calves,w} ≥ F_calves(|D^leg|) (DER-04).

metric.compute: stairway weeks with calves trained and weekly_sets_by_group.calves < meta.targets.calves_floor

rules.title: Which line carries a group's floor
rules.plain: hips → the hamstrings line (glutes when glutes is a Focus line); shoulders → the shoulders line; the others their own line. A pain-reduced line's group is not floored (pain wins).
rules.formal: carrier(g) per volume.floor.carriers; pain(l) ⇒ grp(l) ∉ floored.

rules.title: Field athletes: chest, back, shoulders floored; arms credit-only
rules.plain: For competitive field athletes the floor of 10 applies to chest, back, shoulders and glutes too (R2-VOL-06 over UNI-02); biceps and triceps stay credit-only (no direct station unless a Focus muscle or the sport writes direct sets).
rules.formal: modifier = field_off ⇒ fill[biceps, triceps] = credit; other groups floored.

value.status: D-03 narrowed (v1.2 review): glutes + side delts floored for athletes

metric.compute: as T2-FLR-01 restricted to field athletes

rules.title: Deficit of a listed below-floor group (minimize)
rules.plain: For a group the policy keeps BELOW_FLOOR (work lift only) or a class lift, the shortfall under 10 is minimized - never hidden.
rules.formal: min Σ_{g: state_g = BELOW_FLOOR} Σ_w max(0, F − Q^main_{g,w}).

metric.compute: Σ (10 − main_sets_by_group[g])+ over trained_below_floor groups

rules.title: Week 1 is planned from the structure, never below the floor
rules.plain: The template's structural minimum (every station at its minimum sets) fixes week 1's floor; a group whose structure puts it above its start trains on fewer days (each with 2 exercises) rather than starting at its ceiling.
rules.formal: Q_{g,1} = Σ_{d: z_{g,d}=1} Σ_{s} n_{s,1} c_g ≥ F; if Q_{g,1}^{struct} > S_g then reduce |{d: z_{g,d} = 1}| (keep 2-4 per remaining day).

value.note: a group whose 2 x 2 minimum on every day is above its week-1 target is trained on fewer days, each with 2 exercises

metric.compute: trained lines whose week-1 sets ≥ their ceiling − minimum climb

rules.title: Never down: planned targets and weekly sets of trained groups never drop
rules.plain: Inside a stairway block a line's planned target never drops and a trained group's weekly sets never drop by a set or more (half a set of quarter-credit rounding allowed).
rules.formal: T_l(w) ≥ T_l(w−1);  Q_{g,w} ≥ Q_{g,w−1} − 0.5 for trained g.

metric.compute: (group, week) pairs with weekly_sets_by_group dropping ≥ 0.5 + ε; target_by_muscle drops

rules.title: Minimum climb (never flat)
rules.plain: Every trained group gains at least 2 whole sets over the block (calves 1, a non-carrier line 1, 1 in a block of 7 weeks or less; a below-floor group 1).

value.status: PROPOSED (2-set climb; 1 set in blocks of 7 weeks or less)

metric.compute: trained groups with weekly_sets_by_group[N] − [1] < mc − 0.5

rules.title: No long holds; the second half climbs; the main days carry the climb
rules.plain: In blocks of 8+ weeks a trained big group with a planned climb of 3+ sets gains half a set or more after the halfway week and never holds its sets (within half a set) for more than half the block + 1 week; the main-day total holds for at most half the block; the week total never stays flat two weeks in a row. The climb must sit on the main days, not only on the optional day.
rules.formal: N ≥ 8 ∧ big(g) ∧ climb_g ≥ 3 ⇒ Q_{g,N} − Q_{g,h} ≥ 0.5 ∧ longest_hold_g ≤ h + 1;  longest_hold(Tot^main) ≤ 0.5·N;  ¬(Tot_w = Tot_{w−1} = Tot_{w−2}).

value.r2_status: PROPOSED (fix round 2 / F1, E-136): H21 reads the main days too; the main-day total holds for at most half the block

value.note: placed sets follow the planned T(w): never more than 1 set above in week 1, never 1 or more behind (unless a schedule warning names the muscle); the week total never stays flat two weeks in a row; no "hold" without a check-in

metric.compute: Σ over trained big groups of max(0, longest hold run − (h + 1)) + flat-second-half count + main-total hold excess

rules.title: The last week is the hardest; on 12 weeks the last four are the hardest
rules.plain: The weekly resistance total peaks in the last week; on a 12-week block every one of weeks 9-12 is at least every week of 1-8 ("the last 4 weeks are going to be brutal"); the main-day total rises over the block.
rules.formal: Tot_N = max_w Tot_w;  N = 12 ⇒ min_{w ≥ 9} Tot_w ≥ max_{w ≤ 8} Tot_w;  Tot^main_N > Tot^main_1.

metric.compute: blocks failing the rule (total_resistance_sets, total_main_sets)

rules.title: The stairway shape: small steps to the halfway week, bigger after it
rules.plain: About 3 % a week until the halfway week, about 5 % after it - one rule for every person, never by muscle size; every line's early steps are never larger than its late steps.
rules.formal: s_w = 0.03 (w ≤ h), 0.05 (w > h); ∀l: max_{w ≤ h} step_l(w) ≤ min_{w > h} step_l(w).

metric.compute: lines whose largest planned early step exceeds the smallest late step

rules.title: λ peak anchoring: the peak lands in the last week
rules.plain: Each line's steps are scaled by one λ so it reaches its (time-held) ceiling exactly in the last week; λ never above 1 today (so a line whose ceiling is far peaks below it, still in the last week - open item C-01).
rules.formal: λ_l per DEF-10 with C̃_l; λ_l ≤ λ_max (= 1); T_l(N) = min(C̃_l, S_l·G(N)).
sources: R3-VOL-04 ("reaches its ceiling exactly in the last week")

metric.compute: trained lines whose max weekly sets occur before week N and exceed week N

rules.title: Whole sets track the planned stairway ("round up, round down")
rules.plain: Whole weekly sets follow the planned T(w): each set lands in the week its planned target passes the half set, the last in the last week; never more than 1 set above the plan in week 1 or 1+ set behind it; no week without a step where a neighbour holds two.
rules.formal: min Σ_{l,w} |V^dir_{l,w} − T_l(w)| s.t. V^dir integer, non-decreasing, V^dir_{l,N} = C̃_l;  the optimum is round_half_up(T_l(w)) whenever that series respects T0-STW-03 (SF-1).

value.status: PROPOSED (F1, E-85): whole sets follow round-half-up of the planned T(w) (the coach: "you round up, you round down")
value.r2_status: PROPOSED (fix round 2 / F1, E-146): a whole-set schedule per block - each set in the week its planned T(w) passes the half set, the last in the last week, the 7 % weekly limit, no week without a step where a neighbour holds two (was half_up, E-85)

value.note: placed sets follow the planned T(w): never more than 1 set above in week 1, never 1 or more behind (unless a schedule warning names the muscle); the week total never stays flat two weeks in a row; no "hold" without a check-in

sources: VOL-06 ("you round up, you round down")

metric.compute: Σ |weekly_sets_by_line[l] − target_by_muscle[l]| over trained lines and weeks (direct sets)

rules.title: Start from the larger of the table start and the week-1 sets; no restart at exercise blocks
rules.plain: The stairway climbs from S_l = max(start, week-1 sets) (so no line runs flat while its target catches up) and runs through the whole block across exercise-block boundaries.
rules.formal: S_l = max(start_l, V_{l,1});  T_l continuous over w ∈ W_b.

metric.compute: trained lines whose weekly sets drop at an exercise-block start

rules.title: Stair level rises every week; Focus does not slow the others
rules.plain: The displayed level rises every stairway week (2 → 11). A Focus muscle is a small bias inside a balanced plan: every other trained line keeps its own steps (the 3 % cap on the others only under the optional coach priority push).
rules.formal: level(w) > level(w−1);  focus.slow_others = false ⇒ λ_l independent of Focus.

metric.compute: weeks whose stair_level does not rise

rules.title: Timed circuits climb by work seconds
rules.plain: Bootcamp circuits climb by their work seconds (35 → 50 s) along the planned steps, rounded to 1 s and rising every week while below the top, each step inside the weekly ceiling; rounds fixed by session length.
rules.formal: work_s(w) = round(35·Π(1 + λ s_w)), work_s(N) = 50, work_s(w) > work_s(w−1) while < 50, work_s(w)·Tot_w ≤ 1.10·work_s(w−1)·Tot_{w−1}.

metric.compute: circuit weeks whose work does not rise or rises > 10 %

rules.title: The athletic stairway: doses climb with the block and never drop
rules.plain: Contacts, throws, cuts, sprint metres and Olympic sets climb low → high across a stairway block (the sport's weekly ranges), never drop inside it, and the end-test week holds the week before; a week never plans more than a later week can hold.
rules.formal: ∀k, w ∈ stairway: A_{k,w} ≥ A_{k,w−1};  A_{k,w} ≤ min_{w′ > w} cap_{k,w′};  test week: A_{k,N} = A_{k,N−1}.

value.status: PROPOSED (v1.2 review; B2: capacity scaling, climb, test-week hold, both legs counted)

metric.compute: (key, week) pairs with athletic_budget.planned dropping inside a stairway block

rules.title: Plyometric share ramps from block start to block end
rules.plain: The share of jump and throw work that is plyometric climbs from (end − 15 points) at the block start to the sport's end share (75 / 60 / 50 / 40 / 25 %), held within 5 points each week.
rules.formal: |share_w − share*(w)| ≤ 0.05, share*(w) = (end − 0.15) + progress(w)·0.15.

metric.compute: weeks with |athletic_budget.planned_share − target share| > 0.05

rules.title: Days within the chosen minutes
rules.plain: Minimize the minutes over the chosen session length on every non-test day; the 10 % band of T1-POL-02 is a hard limit for the minimums, and a day over 1.25 x while anything is still cuttable is an error. Test-week days may run long with a warning.
rules.formal: min Σ_{d,w} max(0, Min_{d,w} − μ_d)  s.t. Min_{d,w} ≤ φ·μ_d (T1-POL-02);  Min_{d,w} ≤ 1.25·μ_d hard unless nothing is cuttable.

metric.compute: Σ max(0, est_minutes − minutes_limit) over non-test days; also counts > 1.10x and > 1.25x

rules.title: Session lengths and defaults
rules.plain: Allowed lengths 30 / 45 / 60 / 75 / 90 / 105 / 120 min (over 90 for competitive athletes only); defaults: athletes, bodybuilders, powerlifters 90 (max 120), general and fat loss 60, bootcamp 45, non-competitive athletic 60, older / injured 60.
rules.formal: μ_d ∈ minutes_allowed; μ > 90 ⇒ competitive.

metric.compute: plans with a session length outside the allowed list

rules.title: Bootcamp and class formats keep their own minutes
rules.plain: Bootcamp: 35-45 min, 3-5 rounds x 30-50 s, 5-7 stations (engine: two circuits of 4-6 stations); CrossFit class: warm-up → light core → skill → strength / power → WOD (10-20 min).
rules.formal: format = bootcamp ⇒ Min_d ∈ [35, 45] (by length); rounds ∈ [3,5], work_s ∈ [30,50].

value.status: stairway in rounds and seconds PROPOSED

metric.compute: bootcamp days outside 35-45 min (for a 45-min choice)

rules.title: Direct sets never above the line ceiling (helper spill-over ≤ 1)
rules.plain: The stairway never places a direct set above a line's (time-held) ceiling; helper credit from other lines may carry the weekly total up to about 1 set over, reported, never chased.
rules.formal: V^dir_{l,w} ≤ C̃_l;  V_{l,w} ≤ C̃_l + 1 (soft above C̃_l).

params.name: cap rule
params.value: cap = max(round_half_up(cap[m][L] x factor), start + round_half_up((cap[m][L] - start[m][L]) x factor)); priority caps and own-sets caps unscaled; never above priority.absolute_cap (Pro setting excepted); finally cap >= start

metric.compute: Σ max(0, weekly_sets_by_line[l] − cap[l] − 1) over lines and weeks

rules.title: How a ceiling is computed
rules.plain: Level ceilings 14 / 22 / 25 for every line (abs 16 / 20 / 20); scaled goals keep their level growth room above the real start (cap = max(round(cap x f), start + round((cap − start_table) x f))); Focus + F bounded by 18 / 26 (chest 28) / 30; completed blocks + 1 each (≤ 25 / 30); calves of field / court athletes start + 2; never below start; never above 30.
rules.formal: C_l = min(30, max(S_l, prio_bound(focus(max(rhu(cap·f), S_l + rhu((cap − start⁰)·f))) + k_cycles)));  calves (athletes) = S + 2.

params.name: cap rule
params.value: cap = max(round_half_up(cap[m][L] x factor), start + round_half_up((cap[m][L] - start[m][L]) x factor)); priority caps and own-sets caps unscaled; never above priority.absolute_cap (Pro setting excepted); finally cap >= start

rules.title: Absolute ceiling 30 sets a week for any line (Pro setting excepted)
rules.plain: "More than 30 sets per week of a muscle group should probably be for a very advanced person": no line passes 30 on all days with helper credit; only a coach-set Pro setting (L3, one muscle, up to 35) passes it.
rules.formal: V_{l,w} ≤ 30 ∀l, w (Pro: one l, ≤ 35, L3, coach).

metric.compute: line-weeks with weekly_sets_by_line > 30

rules.title: Ceiling attainment: as close to the ceiling as the minutes allow, in the last week
rules.plain: Each trained line reaches its ceiling in the last week when the time holds it; otherwise the highest peak the time holds, listed as "a lower peak" (trained groups only). Below time fit (T4): the 10 % band is never spent on extra height.
rules.formal: min Σ_{l trained} (C_l − C̃_l), C̃_l ≤ P^time_l = the most the minutes hold at μ (this inventory's reading of the tier order, C-16; the engine today places up to φ·μ, D-47).

metric.compute: Σ (cap[l] − weekly_sets_by_line[l][N])+ over trained lines

rules.title: Per-session sets per line ≤ 11 (Focus / priority 14)
rules.plain: A line's fractional sets in one session stay at or below about 11 (14 for a Focus or priority line).
rules.formal: Σ_{s ∈ S_d} n_{s,w} c_l(x_s) ≤ 11 (14 if l ∈ Focus).

metric.compute: (day, line) with > 11 (14) fractional sets

rules.title: Focus muscles: at most 2, +1 to +3 each
rules.plain: At most two Focus muscles; each +F extra weekly sets (default 2, range 1-3) on start and ceiling, its exercise first in its session; the coach-only priority push (+4 / +4 / +6, others ≤ 3 %) is an optional setting, off by default.
rules.formal: |Focus| ≤ 2; F ∈ [1,3]; V_{l,w} − V^{balanced}_{l,w} = F for l ∈ Focus.

metric.compute: plans with > 2 Focus muscles or a Focus add outside 1-3

rules.title: Athletic budget never exceeded
rules.plain: A week's planned dose of a key stays within its target x 1.25 + one set's maximum (reactive + ballistic jumps as one budget); Olympic within 1.5 x (or the exposures' minimum); per-set doses within their bounds; stations per day: COD 2, sprint 1, throws 2, ankle 1; single-leg contacts ≤ 6 a leg (low hops 15); weekly contact rise ≤ 20 %.
rules.formal: A_{k,w} ≤ 1.25·Â_{k,w} + max_per_set_k;  olympic ≤ 1.5·Â;  a_{s,w} ∈ [per_set_min_k, per_set_max_k];  A_{contacts,w} ≤ 1.2·A_{contacts,w−1}.

metric.compute: (key, week) with athletic_budget.planned > 1.25 x targets + one set

rules.title: Athletic budget attainment (and an honest warning when the minutes cannot hold it)
rules.plain: Plan each key as close to its weekly target as the stations and minutes hold, keeping the target's shape (one scale factor per exercise block); a stairway peak under 60 % of the sport target must be told (warning.athletic_capacity), jumps and ankle work told apart.
