structural_facts.title: The coach's rounding is the optimal monotone integer tracker
structural_facts.text: T_l(w) is non-decreasing (every factor 1 + λ s_w ≥ 1), and round_half_up is a non-decreasing function, so V^dir_{l,w} = round_half_up(T_l(w)) is automatically monotone, has |V − T| ≤ 0.5 (the best possible L∞ error for integers), and lands on C̃_l in week N when C̃_l is an integer. "You round up, you round down" (VOL-06) therefore needs no bank or smoothing logic on the direct sets; the only source of non-integers is quarter-set helper credit, which a solver should hold fixed per exercise choice and add on top (T5-CAP-01 tolerates +1). Caveat: while ΔT ≤ 1 a week the rounded series rises by at most one set a week; above about 20 sets a late 5 % step exceeds 1 set and the rounded series can jump 2 in one week - the placed limit (T0-STW-03) then spreads it to the neighbouring week.

structural_facts.title: λ is unique and cheap
structural_facts.text: f(λ) = S·(1 + 0.03λ)^{h−1}·(1 + 0.05λ)^{N−h} is strictly increasing on [0, 1], so for S < C̃ < S·G(N) the root is unique; 60 bisection steps (D-18) or 5 Newton steps on ln f give it to machine precision. Reference values (12 §3.7.1): N = 12, L2 big 15 → 22: λ = 0.87 (2.60 % / 4.33 %); L3 big 20 → 25: λ = 0.50; L1 10 → 14: λ = 0.76. A λ above 1 (late steps up to 7 %) is the only way small lines reach 22 / 25 in 12 weeks (C-01).

structural_facts.title: VOL-07 is a closed-form apportionment
structural_facts.text: Given the sets N_{d,l} a line gets on a day and its k exercises in session order, the coach's staircase (starting from a staircase week-1 vector such as 2/2/2 or 3/2/2) is n_i = ⌊N/k⌋ + [i ≤ N mod k] (2/2/2 → 3/2/2 → 3/3/2 → 3/3/3 → 4/3/3), i.e. Hamilton / largest-remainder apportionment with ties broken by session order, clipped at the per-exercise maximum by water-filling. The isolation-never-passes-a-compound rule (E-87) holds automatically because compounds come first in the session order.

structural_facts.title: R3-VOL-03 is the same apportionment across exposures
structural_facts.text: For a day type with two exposures the sets a line adds over week 1 split ⌈Δ/2⌉ / ⌊Δ/2⌋ with the earlier day taking the odd set (Monday first, then Thursday). Combined with SF-3, the whole per-day, per-exercise allocation of a line is a deterministic function of its weekly direct total V^dir_{l,w}, its days and its exercise order. The free dosing decisions therefore collapse to (state_g, z_{g,d}, the exercise layout per exercise block, V^dir_{l,w}) - at most 9 lines x 16 weeks = 144 integers per block plus the layout.

structural_facts.title: Everything except group credit and superset rest is linear in the sets
structural_facts.text: With the exercise layout fixed, credits are constants (c_l(x) = min(1, Σ) is evaluated per exercise, not per set), so V and Q are linear in n. Straight-set minutes are linear in n. A superset with equal sets costs n·(Σ work + max rest), linear; with unequal sets n1 ≥ n2 it costs n2·(w1 + w2 + max(r1, r2)) + (n1 − n2)·(w1 + r1) - linear once the order is fixed, and SF-3 fixes it. So, per layout, the dosing problem is an integer linear program; the hard part is the combinatorial layout / state choice, not the arithmetic.

structural_facts.title: A capacity lower bound prunes the R3-SES-02 search
structural_facts.text: For a candidate trained set Y: Σ_{d ∈ D^main} φ·μ_d ≥ Σ_d overhead_d + Σ_{g ∈ Y} [F_g·τ^min_g + co^min_g·|days(g)|·2] + Σ_{kept fixed blocks} minutes, where overhead_d = warm-up + core opener (+ skill), τ^min_g = the cheapest per-set minutes of g's legal exercises with the superset discount (a bilateral compound paired with an upper compound: (0.75 + 0.75 + 1.5) / 2 = 1.5 min a set; straight 2.25), co^min = 0.5 in a pair. Any Y that fails the bound is infeasible without building it; for the peak week add each group's minimum climb. The bound is necessary, not sufficient (pairing, axial and day assignment can still fail).

structural_facts.title: Where the minutes go in a 2 x 45 week (worked numbers, model time parameters)
structural_facts.text: Per straight set: bilateral compound 2.25 min, unilateral compound 3.0, isolation 1.85, core 1.5, joint care 1.35, throw 1.6, Olympic 3.0; warm-up 8; core opener 5.5 as a pair (8 straight); fit limit 45 x 1.10 = 49.5. Day with 4 big movers at the floor (5 sets each a day: knee + pull pair 3 + 3, hip + push pair 3 + 3, second exercises isolation + compound 2 + 2, all paired): 46.9 min - fits; the same at the peak (+2 sets a group a week): 52.9 - does not. Calves (pinned, 3 sets) + hips + quads at the peak (12 a week each), straight sets: 49.05 - fits. One throw station (2 sets) + one Olympic piece (2 sets) + two joint-care items cost 15.9 min a day. So for the coach's own example the decisive question is not the volume math but which fixed blocks (athletic, power, joint care, core) stay inside 45 minutes: without them three groups climb; with all of them about one does. Sample 08 shows it: at fix round 1 it trained hips only (10 → 13); the fix-round-2 regeneration (samples/plans, 2026-10-10 00:57 UTC) keeps quads and hips below the floor on their work lifts (4 → 6 and 4.5 → 5.75 sets), calves 7 → 8, back as one 2-set pattern station and no press at all, with main days at 44-49 min for 45. Illustrative composition; computed with rules.time_model.

structural_facts.title: Greedy in keep order is exact only for downward-closed feasibility
structural_facts.text: Adding groups one by one in π order and keeping each that still fits yields the lexicographic optimum exactly when the feasible family of trained sets is downward closed (removing a group never breaks another). Here it is not: (a) hip + push / knee + pull pairing makes a lower group depend on its upper partner; (b) helper credit crosses groups (squats give hips 0.25, rows give rear delts the V18 minimum, presses give triceps); (c) the axial rule and 2-4 per day constrain which days a group can take; (d) a kept group's day assignment changes the minutes left for later groups. An exact lex-max therefore needs search with re-checks, not a single greedy pass; with ≤ 8 groups and 4 states the space is ≤ 65,536 vectors and π-ordered depth-first search with the SF-6 bound prunes most of it.

structural_facts.title: Training frequency is a dosing decision
structural_facts.text: Week-1 sets of a group are at least 2 exercises x 2 sets on each day it is trained: Q_{g,1} ≥ 4·|{d: z_{g,d} = 1}|. A group on 3 full-body days starts at 12+ sets - above an L1 start of 10 and 2 sets from the L1 ceiling 14, which leaves almost no stairway (RECHECK 02 "each group can only gain 2 sets in 12 weeks"). Choosing z_{g,d} (how many days a group is trained) must therefore be part of the dosing optimization, not fixed by the template (E-83 does it as a repair).

structural_facts.title: A two-stage split is exact if stage 1 uses the stage-2 minutes formula
structural_facts.text: Stage 1 (states, days per group, weekly line totals V^dir_{l,w}) and stage 2 (exercises, per-slot sets, order, supersets) separate cleanly when stage 1 checks time with the closed-form allocation of SF-3 / SF-4 and the per-layout linear minutes of SF-5: every stage-1 solution then has a stage-2 realization with the same minutes. Without that link (today: volume targets first, time cuts after) the stages fight - the patch-on-patch failures of the review log.
